## `slot`

Run builds on one shared pool of build slots.

`slot <command…>` sends the command to the slot daemon, which queues it until enough slots are free, runs it, streams its output back and exits with its code. Every build that goes through the daemon shares one GNU-make jobserver, so cargo, rustc and make draw parallelism from the same pool and the machine is never oversubscribed.

```text
slot [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

- `--local`: Run the command here, without the daemon (default `false`)
- `--tokens`: Slots the job holds, in place of the count slot derives from the command. For work the daemon cannot see, such as a script that starts `docker run --cpus 4`: `slot --tokens 4 ./build.sh`. The daemon caps it at the slots in circulation (the pool less the headroom), so the job never waits forever. Ignored with `--local` (env `SLOT_TOKENS`)
- `--fetch`: With `SLOT_HOST` set: after the job exits 0, copy PATH back from the build server into the checkout. PATH is relative to the repository root; `target/…` is read from the job's target directory on the server. Repeat for more paths. Without `SLOT_HOST` the output is already here and this does nothing

### `slot serve`

Run the daemon: the slot pool, the job queue and the web UI

```text
slot serve [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: Unix socket clients connect to (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--http`: Web UI address; `off` disables it (default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--tokens`: Build slots in the pool (jobserver tokens); default: the number of CPUs
- `--go-tokens`: Slots a go job holds; go's -p is set to match (default `4`)
- `--test-threads`: Threads a test runner in a job may use when the caller sets none: `RUST_TEST_THREADS`, `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS` and `GOMAXPROCS` (go jobs get their slot count). Default: a quarter of the pool, at least 2
- `--cpu-quota`: Whether a headroom also sets systemd `CPUQuota` on the daemon unit, a hard cap on every job together; `false` keeps only the token limit (default `true`)
- `--state-dir`: Jobserver FIFO and job log
- `--ws-root`: Where remote clients sync workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/ws`)
- `--cache-root`: Target dirs and caches for synced workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/cache`)
- `--memory-max`: systemd `MemoryMax` per job, for example 24G
- `--keep-jobs`: Finished jobs kept in memory and shown in the UI (default `500`)
- `--cpu-weight`: systemd `CPUWeight` for every job (interactive apps default to 100); 0 leaves it unset. Applied to the daemon's own unit at start (default `20`)
- `--call-headroom`: Call mode: headroom while a call uses the microphone or the camera, percent; 0 turns call mode off. `slot headroom --call` changes it at run time and that value is kept (default `40`)
- `--call-off-after`: Seconds without capture after which a call counts as ended and the headroom goes back (default `120`)
- `--call-ignore`: Applications whose capture is not a call (level meters, mixers), comma-separated; replaces the default list (default `claude,pavucontrol,pwvucontrol,easyeffects,helvum,qpwgraph,coppwr,noisetorch`)
- `--sccache-watch`: Watch this user's sccache servers and write back the jobserver tokens a server lost, once it had none free for 60 s while compiles waited; `false` turns the watchdog off (default `true`)
- `--min-free-disk`: A job waits while the filesystem of its directory or of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` has less free space than this, GB; 0 turns it off (default `25`)
- `--min-free-memory`: A job waits while available memory, less what jobs that started in the last 30 s still take, is below its expected peak (from earlier runs) plus this, GB; 0 turns it off. A job alone in the pool runs anyway (default `4`)
- `--upgrade-hold`: After `systemctl --user reload slot`, the longest time no new job starts while jobs still run, seconds. Then jobs start again, and the next hold begins when the running jobs are expected to end within it (from earlier runs of the same command) or none runs. 0 never holds (default `60`)
- `--cache-budget`: For remote clients: GB the target directories of synced workspaces may take together. Before a remote job starts, the least recently used target directories and their source copies are deleted while the total is over this, or while the disk has less than `--min-free-disk` free; a workspace with a queued or running job is kept. 0: no budget, only the disk floor evicts (default `0`)
- `--evict-below`: When the filesystem of a local Cargo target directory has less free space than this, GB, delete target directories that jobs built into, least recently built first, until it has 10 GB more. Directories of a repository with a queued or running job, or built in the last 2 h, are kept. 0 turns it off (default `40`)
- `--evict-dry-run`: Only report in the journal and `slot status` which target directories eviction would delete; `false` deletes them (default `true`)
- `--handover`: On `systemctl --user reload slot`, re-execute at once and hand the running and queued jobs, their slots and their clients to the new binary; `false`, or a new binary older than 0.11.0, uses the `--upgrade-hold` rule instead (default `true`)

### `slot proxy`

Bridge stdin/stdout to the daemon's socket (remote clients run this over ssh)

```text
slot proxy [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: The daemon's socket (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)

### `slot shell`

ssh forced command for a build server: runs only the sync, fetch, proxy and cancel steps named in `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`

```text
slot shell [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: The daemon's socket, for `slot proxy` (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--state-dir`: The daemon's state directory
- `--ws-root`: Where remote clients sync workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/ws`)
- `--cache-root`: Target dirs of synced workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/cache`)

### `slot run`

Run a build command; use this when the command's name is also a slot subcommand

```text
slot run [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...
```

- `--tokens`: Slots the job holds, as `slot --tokens N`; capped at the slots in circulation. Ignored with `--local`
- `<COMMAND>`: The command and its arguments

### `slot status`

Show the pool and every queued and running job

```text
slot status [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot headroom`

Show or set the headroom: the share of the CPU kept free for you

```text
slot headroom [OPTIONS] [PERCENT]
```

- `<PERCENT>`: New headroom, percent, 0 to 50; without it, prints the current one
- `--call`: Headroom during a call, percent, 0 to 50; 0 turns call mode off
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot cancel`

Cancel a queued or running job you submitted; a running job's processes get SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 s

```text
slot cancel [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

- `<ID>`: Job id, as `slot status` shows it (`#12` or `12`)

### `slot sessions`

List agent sessions that build outside the pool, with their commands

```text
slot sessions [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--window`: Seconds of history to average (default `60`)
- `--min-cores`: Leave out sessions below this many cores outside slot, unless a command of theirs runs now; builds outside any agent session are left out below it in any case (default `0.5`)
- `--json`: Print JSON instead of text (default `false`)

### `slot hook`

Agent hooks: refuse a build command that would run outside the pool

```text
slot hook [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `slot hook claude-pre-tool-use`

Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook for the Bash tool: reads the event on stdin and exits 2 with the `slot` command to run when the command builds or tests outside the pool. `SLOT_HOOK=warn` adds the advice as context instead of refusing; `SLOT_HOOK=off` allows everything

```text
slot hook claude-pre-tool-use [OPTIONS]
```
